checks.label: You always need an arrow from the origin to a point of the line and an arrow parallel to the line: on every line screen, the line is drawn through its start along its direction, and for every setting of t the dot sits at the start plus t lots of the direction
Every plane has a vector orthogonal to it, its normal: wherever the tip of n is dragged, the tile turns with it, so both edges of the tile stay square to n and every corner reads 0
The reading n · (r − p) is 0 exactly when the test point lies in the plane, above 0 on the side n points to and below 0 on the other, wherever r is dragged, and the readout shows that value

Every worked number is right: (2, 5, 0) at t = 2; (3, 7, 0) at t = 3, with 3v = (3, 6, 0) and 3p + v = (1, 5, 0); B − A = (2, 4, −2) and the midpoint (2, 2, 1); (3, 2, 0) and A + B = (7, 4, 2); the step (1, 0, −1) reads 0, p + n reads 9 and the origin −9; n · p = 9, |n| = 3, 9 ÷ 3 = 3, foot (2, 1, 2); (1, 3, 2) gives 9; d = 1 for (1, 2, 0) and (3, −1, 2); u × w = (2, 1, 2); (1, 1, 0) × (0, 1, 1) = (1, −1, 1); −8, n · v = 4, t = 2; (1, 2, 2) and t = 2.5; n · n = 9; the two planes meet along (1, 1, 3) + t(2, 2, −3); the worked example 6x + 3y + 2z = 6, |n| = 7, about 0.86
Each puzzle's answer comes from the rule, and each wrong answer offered is the slip its hint names
Each puzzle offers three different answers, accepts only the right one, and draws every wrong one in the warning colour
Before Check, no puzzle shows its answer; after a right answer, it does

Each demonstration ends where the lesson says: t = 2 with the dot at (2, 5, 0); t = ½ with the dot at the midpoint (2, 2, 1); the test point back at (2, 1, 2) reading 0; the origin reading −9, 3 from the tile at (2, 1, 2); the paint on every point the dot reaches, with u × w = (2, 1, 2) and the dot reading 0; t = 2 with the dot touching the tile at (2, 5, 0)

While each demonstration plays, the rule holds at every moment: the dot stays on its line, the test point reads n · (r − p) with the sign of its side, the painted dot always reads 0, and the meeting dot's reading climbs by n · v = 4 for each unit of t
In span mode, every setting of s and t puts the dot on the plane, reading 0, and u × w is square to both u and w
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its 3 to 4.5 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s

warnings: SVG labels "p" and "r" are only 2 px apart on one row, so they read as one: leave at least 4 px between them, or label only what differs (at t = ½, and 1 more setting) [at 340 px wide]
